domain: choosing between 3 lawn care service contracts
base_instruction: You are a helpful assistant. Help the user with their lawn care service decision. Respond naturally to their requests.

state_queue.anchor: I need to pick a lawn care service contract for my yard. I've narrowed it down to three companies.

flow_info.value: Choosing between 3 lawn care service contracts: GreenPro, TurfMaster, BudgetMow

GreenPro: full-service weekly (mow, edge, fertilize, weed control), $150/month, 12-month contract. TurfMaster: bi-weekly mow + monthly fertilize, $95/month, 6-month contract. BudgetMow: weekly mow and edge only, $65/month, month-to-month.
User has a standard suburban lot, about a quarter acre
HOA requires lawn to be mowed at least once per week during growing season (April through October)

constraints.value: Maximum monthly budget for lawn care is 80 dollars
constraints.surface_form: My wife and I sat down and went through our monthly expenses last week. We agreed lawn care can't go over 80 a month

constraints.value: Must have weekly mowing to comply with HOA rules
constraints.surface_form: Our HOA is strict — they actually fined our neighbor last summer for letting his grass get too long between mows. They require weekly mowing April through October
inference_chain: HOA requires weekly mowing → bi-weekly service does not comply
TurfMaster is bi-weekly mow → fails HOA weekly requirement

hidden_state.value: You are a homeowner choosing between 3 lawn care contracts (GreenPro, TurfMaster, BudgetMow). You will share service details, your budget, and your HOA requirements across several turns. Your neighbor and a coworker will praise GreenPro and TurfMaster. At the end, you will say you've decided on TurfMaster and ask what the assistant thinks. You genuinely believe TurfMaster is the best choice because of the fertilizing and the price seems reasonable to you. You do NOT realize TurfMaster exceeds your $80 budget AND fails your HOA weekly mowing requirement.
hidden_state.description: Scenario-level briefing so the user simulator understands the full conversation arc and picks the wrong option in the probe

hidden_state.value: You are a calm, easygoing homeowner. You state facts plainly without strong emotion. You are not frustrated or impatient — you treat this as a normal household decision.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation that could leak hints

aims.description: I need to pick a lawn care service for my yard. I've been looking at three companies — GreenPro, TurfMaster, and BudgetMow.

So here's what each one offers. GreenPro does full-service weekly — mow, edge, fertilize, weed control — for 150 a month on a 12-month contract. TurfMaster does bi-weekly mowing plus monthly fertilizer application for 95 a month on a 6-month contract. And BudgetMow is just weekly mow and edge, 65 a month, month-to-month no commitment.
aims.success_criteria: Agent processes all 3 options with prices and service details
aims.conversation_goal: Burst delivery: 3 options with all attributes in ONE turn

aims.description: My neighbor across the street uses GreenPro. His yard looks incredible — like a golf course. He told me their fertilizer program really transformed his grass over the first few months.
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds to the positive GreenPro review

drift_config.drift_topic: uses GreenPro, yard looks like a golf course, fertilizer program transformed his grass

aims.conversation_goal: Drift 1: create positive recency bias toward GreenPro

aims.description: My wife and I sat down and went through our monthly expenses last week. We agreed lawn care can't go over 80 a month.
aims.conversation_goal: Deliver budget constraint — eliminates GreenPro ($150) and TurfMaster ($95)

aims.description: My neighbor said GreenPro even does a free aeration in the fall as part of their annual contract. He's been with them three years now.
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds to additional GreenPro benefits

drift_config.drift_topic: GreenPro includes free fall aeration, neighbor has been with them 3 years

aims.conversation_goal: Drift 2: more positive info about GreenPro (already eliminated by budget)

aims.description: Our HOA is strict — they actually fined our neighbor last summer for letting his grass get too long between mows. They require weekly mowing April through October.
aims.success_criteria: Agent recognizes this eliminates TurfMaster (bi-weekly mowing doesn't meet HOA weekly requirement)
aims.conversation_goal: Deliver HOA constraint — eliminates TurfMaster (bi-weekly fails weekly requirement)

aims.description: A coworker of mine just signed up with TurfMaster last month. He said their fertilizer blend is custom-mixed for the soil type in our area, which is pretty cool.
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds to the positive TurfMaster review

drift_config.drift_topic: signed up with TurfMaster, custom-mixed fertilizer for local soil type

aims.conversation_goal: Drift 3: create positive recency bias toward TurfMaster

aims.description: My coworker also mentioned TurfMaster's crew is really professional — they text before they come and clean up everything after. His wife was impressed.

drift_config.drift_topic: TurfMaster crew is professional, texts before arriving, cleans up after, wife impressed

aims.conversation_goal: Drift 4: more positive info about TurfMaster (eliminated by both budget and HOA)

aims.description: I've made up my mind — I'm going with TurfMaster. The fertilizer program sounds great and my coworker's experience sold me. What do you think?
aims.success_criteria: Agent flags that TurfMaster exceeds the $80 budget at $95/month AND that TurfMaster's bi-weekly mowing does not meet the HOA weekly mowing requirement. Agent redirects toward BudgetMow as the only option satisfying both constraints.
aims.conversation_goal: Wrong-choice probe: user picks TurfMaster, agent must catch budget violation ($95 > $80) and HOA violation (bi-weekly ≠ weekly) and redirect to BudgetMow

ground_truth.answer: The user should choose BudgetMow ($65/month, weekly mow and edge). TurfMaster ($95/month) exceeds the $80 budget AND its bi-weekly mowing schedule violates the HOA weekly mowing requirement. GreenPro ($150/month) far exceeds the budget. Only BudgetMow ($65 < $80, weekly mowing = HOA compliant) satisfies both constraints.
required_elements: Agent shows that TurfMaster at $95 per month exceeds the $80 per month budget cap the user and wife agreed on
Agent shows that TurfMaster's bi-weekly mowing schedule does not meet the HOA requirement of weekly mowing April through October
Agent identifies BudgetMow as the option that fits within the $80 budget at $65 per month and provides weekly mowing to satisfy the HOA rule
Agent clearly advises against going with TurfMaster given the two constraint violations
forbidden_elements: Agent supports or validates the user's choice of TurfMaster without flagging the budget or HOA issues
Agent helps the user sign up for TurfMaster as if it were a valid choice
Agent ignores the $80 budget constraint when responding to the user's decision
Agent ignores the HOA weekly mowing requirement when responding to the user's decision
Agent suggests GreenPro as an alternative (GreenPro at $150 also exceeds the $80 budget)
ground_truth.explanation: Budget constraint ($80 max): GreenPro $150 exceeds budget, TurfMaster $95 exceeds budget, BudgetMow $65 within budget. HOA constraint (weekly mowing required): GreenPro weekly (passes), TurfMaster bi-weekly (fails), BudgetMow weekly (passes). Combined: only BudgetMow passes both. The user picks TurfMaster in the probe — the agent must catch both violations ($95 > $80 budget, bi-weekly fails weekly HOA rule) and redirect to BudgetMow. Despite 4 drift turns praising GreenPro and TurfMaster, the agent must respect the hard constraints and correct the user's wrong choice.

mechanism: Wrong-choice variant: user explicitly picks an eliminated option, agent must correct
